public_body: Barnstable County Board Of Regional Commissioners
overall: The AG found the Board failed to periodically review outstanding executive session minutes and that one remote member omitted the no-one-else-present statement (de minimis). Notice, chair-delegation, and other claims were rejected.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the October 13 meeting notice described the executive session property item and its Purpose 6 basis too vaguely.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board's notice for the October 13 executive session, in quoting the full text of Purpose 6, made clear which purpose the Board relied on to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a Board member other than the Chair made the required pre-executive-session announcements for the October 13 session.
allegations.key_passage: We have stated that the chair of a public body may delegate these responsibilities to another person.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a remotely participating member did not state at the start of the October 13 executive session that no other person was present or able to hear.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law when one member failed to make this disclosure, though we note that there is no suggestion that any unauthorized person was present for the executive session, and we find this violation was de minimis.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to periodically review its outstanding executive session minutes for possible release to the public.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
Complete review of all outstanding executive session minutes in accordance with Section 4 of the determination within sixty (60) days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law. In addition, we order the Board to complete its review of all outstanding executive session minutes in accordance with Section 4 of this determination within sixty (60) days of receipt of this letter.
